acceptance.original_english_fidelity: Accepted: the nonspoken instruction is faithfully translated. All clauses of each of the six Latin stanzas are represented in the plain study English, including the world-ransom and royal/noble-womb predicates; gift, birth, Virgin, earthly sojourn and seed; supper, brothers, legal foods and present self-giving to the twelve; incarnate Word, real bread, flesh, wine/Blood, senses and faith; bowed reverence, old observance/new rite and faith supplying the senses; Father/Son, praise, joyful acclaim, salvation, honor, power, blessing, procession from both, equal praise and final Amen. English line mapping need not duplicate Latin line order. No textual correction requested. Composite hash 5e4b22f6ba9a372b240daa866558fdba02df2b66073716ca8c6d1a0132749e2b; hymn-only hash 8f7311f6b7e86039adcbcb03e6b7cd81ca6c05430d977cf5a13a4e50e69fc0d5.
acceptance.authorship_and_credit: Accepted: the entire active English is original Triptych study English with its own source carrier and notice. It is distinct in phrasing from the retained historical English. The Lasance/Walsh hand missal remains a separately identified human historical witness, not the active translation and not a newly identified individual hymn translator. The superseded hybrid is not accepted for installation.
acceptance.nonspoken_structure: Accepted after R6: the exact Latin instruction words at offset zero are marked as a rubric; its structural terminal newline remains in the body but is excluded from the action span. Original English instruction is similarly marked. Actual owner projection gives Latin action [0,147) and English action [0,152). The six hymn paragraph groups follow and are not part of either action. Both owning structure validators return no errors.
acceptance.stage_boundary: Accepted as a source-grounded interpretation of the named prescription: first four historical hymn stanzas during procession, repeated if necessary, with the last two beginning Tantum ergo at the repository. Rubric 4 literally names Tantum ergo; inclusion of the closing Genitori stanza comes from the independently witnessed complete hymn. No browser performance scheduling or rendered-stage behavior was tested.
